generic_sampling_rules.integer_pk: Sequential integers starting at 1, unique per table, never NULL.
generic_sampling_rules.integer_fk: Uniformly sampled from the parent table's generated primary-key values; nullable FKs get NULL in ~10% of rows.
generic_sampling_rules.varchar_short: Random lowercase alphanumeric strings of length 6-12; near-variants (case flips, one-char edits) for listed literals.
generic_sampling_rules.varchar_name: Random first/last names from a small pool; duplicates allowed on DISTINCT-targeted columns.
generic_sampling_rules.varchar_password: Random hex strings of the declared length.
generic_sampling_rules.varchar_address: Random street number + street name + newline + city, state, zip.
generic_sampling_rules.enum_flag: Uniformly sampled from the listed enum values.
generic_sampling_rules.null_share: For nullable columns, ~10% NULL; NOT NULL columns never NULL.

generation_specification.uncertainty: author_tutor_ATB enum values inferred from column name (A=author, T=tutor, B=both); original sample shows only numeric codes 331,975,... which are not 3-char enums, so enum is a design choice. No formula links any column to another; all other columns are freely sampled within their domains.

issues.evidence: Specification 'uncertainty' field admits author_tutor_ATB enum values (A/T/B) are inferred from the column name; the original sample shows numeric codes (331, 975, ...) that are not 3-char enums. The declared column is VARCHAR(3), so the enum is a design choice rather than a supported rule.
issues.requested_revision: Mark the author_tutor_ATB enum as an uncertain/design-choice pattern (not a supported semantic rule) in the specification, or drop it. No program change required since the program already implements it as a design choice.

issues.evidence: Specification lists 'Student_Course_Enrolment.student_id' under null_targets and per_column_exceptions null_rows as 'NOT NULL column, no NULLs', yet the schema declares student_id INTEGER NOT NULL. The program's _apply_null_rule skips NOT NULL columns (instance.py checks cm.notnull), so no NULLs are planted — consistent with the schema, but the spec's null_targets entry is contradictory.
issues.requested_revision: Remove Student_Course_Enrolment.student_id (and course_id, which is also NOT NULL) from null_targets, or clarify that null_targets only applies to nullable columns. The program already behaves correctly; this is a spec wording fix.

issues.evidence: Execution feedback shows nullable columns with NULL 0 / n are not present (all listed nullable columns have NULL > 0), so the NULL rule is satisfied. However, the program's _apply_null_rule is applied to every nullable column with rng.random() < 0.5 even when not in SPEC_NULL_TARGETS, which is broader than the spec's null_targets list. This is benign (interface rule requires NULLs in every nullable column) but not explicitly specified.
issues.requested_revision: Document in the specification that the NULL rule applies to all nullable columns (per interface rule 7), not only the listed null_targets, so spec and program agree. No code change needed.

issues.evidence: instance.py _build_enrolments sets date_of_enrolment to a strictly increasing positional_series (step 1800s) regardless of the sampled values, discarding the _sample_column result. This satisfies the 'ties_for_order_limit ASC, no LIMIT' target (no ties) but the spec target says 'ASC, no LIMIT' which is about ordering, not strict uniqueness. The construction is acceptable but the dead _sample_column call is misleading.
issues.requested_revision: Remove the unused _sample_column call for date_of_enrolment or add a comment explaining the positional series is intentional for the ASC ordering target. No behavioral change required.

issues.evidence: writer.py write_generated_rows computes ok[t] twice; the first assignment uses a fragile 'bad' in dir() check and is immediately overwritten by ok[t] = max(0, n - bad[t]). The intermediate line is dead code and the 'bad' counter is only incremented in the fallback path, so ok[t] may overcount if executemany partially succeeds before raising.
issues.requested_revision: Simplify the row-count accounting: remove the dead first assignment and compute ok/bad from a single consistent path (e.g., count rows actually inserted via changes() or per-row fallback). This is a robustness fix, not a blocking error since integrity checks passed (0 violations).

issues.evidence: spec.py plan_parent_histogram contains a stray line 'rng.shuffle_order = None' (assigning an attribute on the Random object) which is a no-op bug. The function is not called anywhere in instance.py (group sizes are planned via plan_group_sizes/materialize_group_plan instead), so it is dead code.
issues.requested_revision: Remove the dead plan_parent_histogram function or fix the stray line. No behavioral impact since it is unused.
